footer.about: A local note-taking app for Windows. Your notes stay on your machine, and they stay files.

meta.title: PandaKeep — local, private note-taking app for Windows
meta.description: A 100% local note-taking app for Windows. No account, no server, no telemetry: your notes stay on your PC as readable Markdown files.

hero.lede: A desktop note-taking app, 100% local. No account, no server, no telemetry: your notes live on your machine and are mirrored as readable Markdown files in Documents/Pensly.
hero.shotAlt: The PandaKeep window: note list on the left, Markdown editor on the right.

write.title: Write
write.i1: Markdown editor (CodeMirror 6) with toolbar and rendered preview.
write.i2: Autosave as you type, pin the notes that matter.
write.i3: Note templates, with {vars} variables filled in on creation.
write.i4: Clickable {task} checkboxes in the preview, and a view that gathers open tasks from every note.

capture.title: Capture fast
capture.i1: An always-on-top mini window, opened with the global shortcut {keys} (configurable) from any application.
capture.i2: By default, each capture is appended to today's daily note as a timestamped bullet. Or becomes a new note, your choice.
capture.i3: Lives in the system tray: closing the window hides it, PandaKeep stays ready.

organize.title: Organise and link
organize.i1: {link} links with title autocompletion, and a backlinks bar under the editor.
organize.i2: Tags with suggestions, one-click filtering from the sidebar.
organize.i3: Folders and notebooks in a tree, mirrored as subfolders on disk.

find.title: Find
find.i1: Instant full-text search (SQLite FTS5), highlighted snippets, operators.
find.i2: Command palette {keys}: jump to a note, create from a template, export, open history…
find.i3: Everything from the keyboard: {n} new note, {f} search, {p} pin, {d} delete.

files.title: Your files, not our cloud.
files.body: Every note is mirrored as a .md file with YAML front matter. The SQLite database stays the source of truth; the folder opens in any editor.
files.i1: Markdown mirror in {path}, folder configurable, rebuilt on launch if it was moved or deleted.
files.i2: Obsidian-compatible syntax, readable in VS Code or any text editor.
files.i3: Optional two-way sync: a file edited outside PandaKeep is imported back.
files.i4: Import an existing Markdown folder, front matter included.
files.i5: Native PDF export, no print dialog.
files.fileLabel: A sample note, exactly as written to disk

security.title: What should stay private does.
security.encBody: A vault protected by a passphrase: key derived with Argon2, content encrypted with AES-GCM. The key stays in memory, never on disk.
security.leakBody: An encrypted note is not exported to the Markdown mirror, and is never sent to an AI.
security.historyBody: A snapshot on every saved change. Compare two versions, restore the right one.
security.warnBody: Without the passphrase, no recovery is possible.

ai.title: AI, if you want it.
ai.lede: Off by default. Once enabled, it suggests how your text continues, in grey, after a short pause.
ai.demoText: Meeting on Thursday: approve the budget and
ai.localBody: Ollama, with one of the two fastest models ({models}). Downloaded from within the app, with help installing Ollama.
ai.cloudBody: Gemini, OpenAI or Mistral with your API key, tested then stored in Windows Credential Manager. Calls are made by the app core: the key never reaches the interface. The only, deliberate, exception to fully local.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: No. PandaKeep installs and runs without any sign-up.
faq.a2: In a SQLite database on your machine, mirrored as Markdown files in Documents/Pensly (folder configurable).
faq.a3: Yes. PandaKeep is open source, under the MIT licence.
faq.q4: Is there a macOS or Linux version?
faq.a4: No. PandaKeep is Windows-only for now.
faq.q5: Does the AI read my notes?
faq.a5: Only if you turn it on. Locally (Ollama), nothing leaves your machine. In the cloud, the text needed for the suggestion is sent to the provider you chose. Encrypted notes are never sent.
faq.q6: What if I forget my passphrase?
faq.a6: Encrypted notes become unrecoverable. That is the point: only you hold the key.

meta.title: Download PandaKeep for Windows
meta.description: The 64-bit Windows installer for PandaKeep, with what to do about the SmartScreen warning and how to check the signature.

download.title: Download PandaKeep
download.lede: One installer, no account, nothing to set up first. Do read the section about the Windows warning though — it will save you a nasty surprise.
download.cardUnavailable: Release details unavailable at build time
download.req2: No account and no permanent connection: PandaKeep works offline.
download.req3: A writable folder for your notes — Documents/Pensly by default, changeable afterwards.
download.step1Body: The file is named Pensly_[version]_x64-setup.exe. It is published in the public releases repository.
download.step2Body: A double-click is enough. The installer asks for no special administrator rights and no account.
download.step3Body: Windows will show a blue screen saying it protected your PC. The section below explains why, and what to do.
download.step4Body: PandaKeep opens, creates the Documents/Pensly folder and lets you write. Ctrl+Shift+N works from the very first note.

smartscreen.title: Windows will show a warning. That is expected.
smartscreen.body: When you run the installer, Windows displays a blue screen reading “Windows protected your PC”, with a “Don't run” button. This is not a virus detection: it is SmartScreen flagging a publisher it does not know yet.
smartscreen.whyBody: PandaKeep is not signed with an Authenticode certificate. Those certificates cost several hundred euros a year and require company identity verification. Until that changes, Windows will keep warning — even though the file is perfectly clean.
smartscreen.how1: Click “More info”, in small text under the message.
smartscreen.afterBody: The warning will not come back for this file. It will return with the next release, until a certificate is in place.
smartscreen.trustTitle: If you would rather not take our word for it
smartscreen.trustBody: That is fair. The next section covers what you can verify, and what you cannot.

verify.title: Checking where the file comes from
verify.body: Every release publishes a .sig file alongside the installer. It is the signature produced by the Tauri updater key — the same key that authorises automatic updates inside the app.
verify.item1: The installer and its signature are published together, on the release page, in a public repository.
verify.item2: If PandaKeep is already installed, the update mechanism checks that signature before installing anything: a binary tampered with in transit is rejected.
verify.item3: The code is MIT licensed: nothing stops you from reading it, or building it yourself.
verify.honestyBody: The .sig file protects the update chain. It is not an Authenticode signature and it will not make the SmartScreen warning go away. The two mechanisms are unrelated.

download.previousBody: Every published release stays available, with its notes and its files.

meta.title: Getting started — PandaKeep
meta.description: Quick start, the full shortcut list, how file-based syncing really works, and importing from Obsidian or Notion.

guide.title: Guide
guide.lede: Enough to be productive in five minutes, then everything else.

start.title: Quick start
start.step1Body: Ctrl+N creates a note. The first line is the title; the rest is Markdown. Saving happens on its own, half a second after your last keystroke.
start.step2Body: Open Documents/Pensly in Explorer: the .md file is already there. That is the whole idea — the note and the file are one and the same.
start.step3Body: Add tags to the note; they end up in the file's YAML front-matter. Ctrl+P pins a note to the top of the list.
start.step4Body: Ctrl+Shift+N opens a small capture window over any application. You type, you close it, it is saved.

shortcuts.title: Shortcuts
shortcuts.caption: PandaKeep keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.global: Quick capture, even outside the app (configurable)
shortcuts.note: The global shortcut is the only one that works when PandaKeep does not have focus. It is also the only one you can redefine.

files.title: How the “sync” works
files.body: PandaKeep does not sync anything. It writes. Those are two different things, and the difference decides what you can expect.
files.step1: You write a note in PandaKeep. It is saved in a local SQLite database.
files.step2: Right after, PandaKeep writes the matching .md file into the notes folder, with its YAML front-matter.
files.step3: If that folder is covered by Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox or any sync tool, that tool handles the rest — exactly as it does for your other documents.
files.warn1: There is no conflict merging. Two machines editing the same note at once will produce a conflict, arbitrated by your sync tool, not by PandaKeep.
files.warn2: Propagation is not instant: it depends entirely on how fast Drive or OneDrive is.
files.warn3: Editing a .md file by hand, outside PandaKeep, is not a supported scenario.

import.title: Coming from Obsidian or Notion
import.body: PandaKeep imports a folder of .md files. An Obsidian vault is already in that format; for Notion, export to Markdown first.
import.obsidianBody: Pick the vault folder, or any subfolder. Existing front-matter is read and the files are taken as they are.
import.notionBody: In Notion: Settings, then Export, in Markdown format. Unzip the archive, then point PandaKeep at the resulting folder.
import.exportBody: Nothing special to do: the notes folder already is the export. For a single note, PDF and plain-text export are available from the app.

comfort.title: Settings
comfort.themeBody: Light or dark, your choice, independently of Windows.
comfort.langBody: French, English and Spanish. On first launch, PandaKeep follows the system language.
comfort.folderBody: Documents/Pensly by default. You can move it, for instance into an already-synced folder.
comfort.updateBody: PandaKeep checks for new releases and installs them after verifying their signature.

meta.title: Privacy — PandaKeep
meta.description: What PandaKeep and this site collect: nothing. Where your notes are stored, and the only outgoing connections.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: Short version: PandaKeep collects nothing, and neither does this site. The details fit on one page.
privacy.app1Body: There is no sign-up. So no email address, no password, no profile, no user database.
privacy.app2Body: PandaKeep sends your notes nowhere. There is no online service where they could be stored.
privacy.app3Body: No usage statistics, no automatic crash reports, no installation identifier.
privacy.app4Body: The update check queries GitHub to compare version numbers and fetch the signed installer. Nothing you write is transmitted.
privacy.storage1: The .md files are in Documents/Pensly, or in the folder you chose.
privacy.storage2: The SQLite database that runs the app is stored locally, on the same machine.
privacy.storage3: PandaKeep encrypts nothing: the files are plain text, protected by your Windows session.
privacy.site1Body: No analytics tool, no advertising cookie, no third-party script. The pages are static and call no server back once loaded.
privacy.site2Body: Your theme choice is kept in the browser's local storage, only to show the site the way you left it; it goes nowhere. The language is carried by the page address (/, /en, /es). No cookie is set.
privacy.site3Body: Installers are hosted by GitHub. Clicking a download link takes you to their servers, under their own privacy policy.
privacy.contactBody: The code and the releases are public. Questions belong in the repository issues.
